text:
Current limitations reflect the implemented bounded capture-and-replay scheme in this repository. Future solutions are proposed development directions, not implemented capabilities or committed delivery dates.

Sources: docs/design.md; docs/application-checkpoints.md (Current boundaries); docs/elf-checkpoint-chains.md; docs/entry-state-analysis.md; docs/context-object-graphs.md; docs/context-buffer-references.md; docs/initialized-context-state.md; tools/contextify_slice.py; tools/slice_checkpoint_codec.py.

Coverage expands through reviewed roots and conservative dependency analysis. State discovery should retain blockers and explicit ownership/lifetime contracts. Model fidelity requires validating return values and observable effects, preferably against the same native build. Object relocation requires IDs, generations and supported lifetimes. Concurrency needs more than a schedule trace: shared-memory observations and included handler effects remain necessary. Additional pause boundaries need a supported stack and CPU-state restoration contract. Exact-build identity remains the default; migration needs an explicit proven compatibility relation. Functional QEMU checks do not establish timing equivalence.

Proposal order: first improve coverage, state discovery and native differential validation. Then extend object lifetimes, loading and safe points. General IRQ/SMP reproduction and cycle validation remain separate milestones.
